reason: The hypothesis synthesizes three separate findings—edge dislocation strengthening (P19, P34), Cu-induced corrosion degradation via segregation (P13, P35), and segregation-driven oxidation impairment (P47)—into a single, non-obvious threshold mechanism where moderate lattice distortion promotes both edge dislocation activity and a homogeneous protective oxide, while excessive distortion (via Cu microalloying) triggers segregation that simultaneously undermines strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance. No single passage proposes this integrated trade-off or the existence of an optimal distortion threshold linking mechanical and environmental properties.
